home.principleTitle: Tools check structure. People decide meaning.
home.principleText: ProductShape can find broken references and changed definitions. It cannot decide whether an idea is true, whether a change is right, or whether implementation is complete.
home.explorerTitle: See the ProductShape model, not a sales demo.
home.explorerText: This repository defines itself with the same product model it asks teams to create. Browse real artifacts and their relationships in a generated, read-only snapshot.
home.architectureText: Explore the twelve arc42 views of the implementation, from package boundaries to publishing and quality evidence.
home.closingText: You do not need a complete model to begin. Start from the knowledge your next change depends on.

product.title: A product definition you can review like code.
product.intro: ProductShape is a command-line reference implementation for Product Definition as Code. Keep accepted product knowledge in your repository, then connect the work that implements it through stable citations.

sections.title: A shared source for product decisions
sections.text: Model actors, journeys, use cases, rules, terms and requirements as Markdown artifacts. Stable identifiers keep references intact when files move.

sections.title: A useful change has a visible path
sections.text: Product Changes propose a future definition. Validate the proposal, review it with people, apply it on a branch, and let a merge accept the new baseline.

sections.title: Drift becomes inspectable
sections.text: Citations bind consumer documents to artifact content. When an artifact changes, verification reports current, stale, tampered or unresolved references.

sections.title: Works with your delivery method
sections.text: Product Definition as Code is SDD-agnostic. ProductShape provides integrations for OpenSpec and Spec Kit while keeping the core product model independent.

product.boundaryText: Validation is structural. It does not judge product truth. AI can help recover or draft knowledge, but people review the meaning and approve every accepted change. Product truth remains in files under version control.
product.brandSource: Read ProductShape and PDaC naming rules
product.initSource: Read the canonical CLI initialization instructions

workflow.title: From product knowledge to delivery, step by step.
workflow.intro: ProductShape gives product knowledge stable structure and links it to the documents that implement it. Your existing repository and review process stay in control.

steps.title: Start where you are
steps.text: Initialize a new product or add ProductShape to an existing repository. For a brownfield system, recover candidate knowledge from evidence; the tool structures the work but does not scan code and invent a model.

steps.title: Write a proposed definition
steps.text: Describe an actor, rule, journey, requirement or term in the change's proposed state. The initial baseline follows the same governed Product Change process as later updates.

steps.title: Check structure
steps.text: Run validation to check schema, IDs, relationships and lifecycle rules. Structural validity is a useful signal, not proof that the definition is semantically complete.

steps.title: Review and accept
steps.text: People decide whether a change is accurate. Apply materializes it on a working branch; a reviewed merge accepts the new baseline.

steps.title: Cite and verify
steps.text: Consumer documents cite accepted artifacts by stable ID and content digest. Verification makes changed or broken references visible for review.

workflow.noteTitle: Keep product and implementation changes connected, not conflated.
workflow.noteText: A Product Change records product intent. The implementation may ship in the same or a later pull request. A merge does not claim the change was implemented, tested, or released.

start.title: A small, governed first step.
start.intro: The quickest useful path is one accepted artifact, one consumer citation, and one visible stale dependency after a change. The commands below use the current supported CLI version, read from the package release metadata at build time.
start.initCode:
npm install --save-dev --save-exact @prodshape/cli@{{version}}
npx --no-install prodshape init
npx --no-install prodshape validate
npx --no-install prodshape change create CHG-INITIAL
start.initText: The CLI starts with a small kernel. Templates and schemas are available on demand; expand the layout only when it helps your team.
start.authorText: Add your first artifacts under the active CHG-INITIAL change, list them in its operations, and validate the proposal. Review its meaning with the people who know the product.
start.acceptText: After a human marks the change approved, apply it on a working branch and open a pull request. The merge accepts the baseline; applying is not acceptance.
start.citeTitle: 4 · Cite the definition in delivery work
start.citeCode:
prodshape inspect ACT-USER
prodshape cite --id ACT-USER --digest <digest>
prodshape citations verify
start.citeText: Store the citation next to the consumer text it grounds. Change the accepted artifact in a later Product Change and verification will report the recorded citation as stale.
start.releaseNote: Commands and capabilities present only on the repository's main branch may be newer than this published package.
